applicant_utility.summary: This award pays an NZ$18,204 annual stipend plus a tuition waiver capped at NZ$35,000 for the thesis year of a first research Master's, but only four awards exist nationally (one per Academic Division) and Otago currently lists funding as unavailable for 2026 in every Division. You cannot apply directly: the eVision application only becomes available through an alert triggered by your admission application or thesis-paper enrolment. With selection weighted heavily on grades, Otago itself only recommends applying with A or A+ grades in the later years of your degree.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International students with near-perfect transcripts who are starting a thesis-only Master's or about to enter the thesis year of a papers-and-thesis Master's at Otago.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure admission (or thesis-paper enrolment) first, since the eVision scholarship alert is triggered by that step and no standalone form exists
Convert your GPA to an Otago equivalent early and aim for the A-range/8 on the Otago scale that successful applications show
If your previous thesis was ungraded, pass/fail, or below 0.25 EFTS, arrange the external thesis assessment from an assessor outside your supervisory team
Confirm current international tuition rates with the International Office and budget any amount above the NZ$35,000 waiver, plus the student services fee and insurance
Recheck the Master's scholarships page before each of the four rounds (1 March, 1 June, 1 September, 1 November), because divisional funding availability changes as candidates submit or withdraw
common_rejection_risks: Grades below the A/A+ range Otago recommends, when only four awards are contested nationally
Already holding a Master's qualification, which breaches the first-qualification rule
Enrolling in a coursework Master's without a thesis component, which is ineligible for this research award
Waiting for a direct application link that does not exist and missing the eVision alert window
Budgeting only for the NZ$35,000 waiver when actual tuition is higher, leaving an unfunded shortfall
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition above the NZ$35,000 waiver cap, the student services fee, insurance, and any living costs beyond the NZ$18,204 stipend.
document_audit: Thesis assessments must be done by someone familiar with the subject who is outside your supervisory team, and must size the work against an Otago Master's thesis or Honours dissertation
For GPA conversion queries, email scholarship.gpa@otago.ac.nz with your CV (with publications), most recent transcript, and thesis examination report if the thesis is ungraded
Do not rely on the waiver until you have confirmed your programme's international tuition rate with the International Office
alerts: The Master's scholarships page states 'Funding is unavailable for 2026' for all four Divisions (Commerce/School of Business, Health Sciences, Humanities, Sciences), and warns divisional dates can change based on submission or withdrawal of current candidates
With only one award per Division per year, availability can vanish between quarterly checks even when the page was recently updated
The scholarship covers only the thesis component for up to 1 year of full-time enrolment, so pre-thesis coursework papers are unfunded
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for admission to the thesis-based Master's, receive the eVision scholarship alert, complete the eVision application, then wait for the next quarterly review round (1 March, 1 June, 1 September or 1 November).

applicant_utility.summary: Otago's flagship doctoral award pays an NZ$34,128 annual stipend for 36 months plus a domestic-rate tuition waiver for the same period (professional doctorate waivers capped at the domestic rate for up to 36 months), excluding the student services fee and insurance. Up to 153 awards go to domestic and international first-time doctoral candidates in the PhD, DClinDent, DMA, DBA or EDd, and the student services fee and insurance remain payable. A strategic review of the doctoral scholarship scheme is underway, so confirm current settings on the funding-announcement page before relying on any detail. Applications run year-round via eVision and need a completed departmental assessment by the first day of the March, June, September or November round.
applicant_utility.best_fit: First-time doctoral candidates (PhD or the named professional doctorates) with strong transcripts and a feasible, well-resourced project; international applicants must fund the gap between the domestic and international tuition rates.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply for admission first and watch for the eVision scholarship alert, since no standalone application exists
Get the departmental assessment completed and submitted by the first day of your target round month (March, June, September or November), not just the eVision form
Convert international grades to an Otago equivalent early; successful applications typically sit in the US-equivalent A range or at 8 on the Otago scale
Budget the international-versus-domestic tuition differential, the student services fee and insurance, none of which the waiver covers
DClinDent applicants: expect the eVision invitation around October with a decision in late November or December of the same year
common_rejection_risks: Not seeking a first doctoral qualification, which the eligibility rules exclude
An incomplete departmental assessment at the round cutoff, even though the eVision form itself was submitted on time
Reapplying without the Scholarships Office's permission after a previous unsuccessful application
Assuming the waiver covers full international tuition, when it is capped at the domestic rate
A project that Divisional panels judge misaligned with strategic priorities or inadequately supported by the supervisory team
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The student services fee, insurance, and for international students any tuition above the domestic rate covered by the waiver.
document_audit: The departmental assessment is a mandatory part of the submission, so agree the timeline with your prospective department well before the round month
Ungraded, pass/fail or sub-0.25-EFTS research components need a thesis assessment from an assessor outside your supervisory team
For GPA conversion help, email scholarship.gpa@otago.ac.nz with a CV (including publications), the most recent transcript, and any thesis examination report
To reapply, email scholarships@otago.ac.nz with your name, student ID and evidence of genuinely new material; the office reactivates the existing eVision application rather than opening a new one
alerts: A strategic review of the doctoral scholarship programme is underway and award settings may change; check the funding-announcement page before applying
Scholarship decisions are normally definitive, and reapplying requires prior permission from the Scholarships Office
The stipend and waiver are tenable for three years of full-time enrolment, so part-time plans do not fit this award
Māori and Pacific doctoral scholarships continue under the current review but with settings still to be confirmed
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for admission, complete the eVision scholarship application triggered by the portal alert, secure the departmental assessment, and submit both by the first day of the March, June, September or November round month for Divisional panel consideration.
